set.body: Build HalfFlow-LM as a deliberate whole-system stress test for ScalaFIM: a small, elegant, cross-compiled T1 nonlinear registration engine that is fast and accurate, while forcing the supporting data structures and kernels in image and Gale to prove their design. Success is not an algorithm demo alone: image must gain allocation-controlled pull, composition, regridding, pyramid, Jacobian, and inverse-error primitives; Gale must be exercised on reusable tiny solves and operator/workspace contracts without absorbing registration-specific stencils. The product target is supplied-affine symmetric midpoint registration with independent JVM+JS oracles, guarded topology and measured inverse error, fair same-initialization ANTs comparisons, cohort accuracy, peak-memory/runtime receipts, and a deliberately narrow public API and code footprint. Performance work is profile-led; FFT, learned features, GPU abstractions, and lower precision remain gated experiments.
